Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) stock is back in focus after the firm launched its 6th Gen EPYC SP7 server processors, which target agentic AI and high performance computing workloads with a new Zen 6 architecture.

Investors have treated Advanced Micro Devices as a high beta way to play AI this year, with the share price up 147.42% year to date and a 1-year total shareholder return of 122.98%, even after a 30 day share price pullback of 8.69% that briefly interrupted the rally.

Scan how other AI infrastructure players stack up against Advanced Micro Devices by reviewing the hand picked 53 AI infrastructure stocks.

The latest surge in Advanced Micro Devices looks tightly linked to EPYC platforms, Helios racks and multi gigawatt AI deals, even as capital swings in and out on Nvidia headlines. Is today's price still aligned with that engine room?

Most Popular Narrative: 39% Undervalued

On the most followed narrative, Advanced Micro Devices is framed as worth $907.32 a share versus the recent $552.90 close, which puts a spotlight on how investors think AI infrastructure could reshape the story. According to Talos, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, the opportunity rests on AMD evolving into a full platform rather than a single product bet.

"The market previously priced AMD as a 'forced choice' spillover. Recent quarters, particularly the massive Data Center revenue run-rates achieved into 2026, have completely shattered this narrative. AMD is no longer just a GPU alternative; it has cemented itself as the definitive 'End to End AI Platform.' With hyperscalers aggressively expanding their infrastructure, AMD is rapidly scaling from a 'Second Player' into the absolute backbone of modern AI data centers."

See why 206 investors see Advanced Micro Devices as 39% undervalued.

Result: Fair Value of $907.32 (UNDERVALUED)

Still, the Advanced Micro Devices story could shift quickly if AI infrastructure spending slows, or if key hyperscaler customers reduce orders or extend deployment timelines.

Find out about the key risks to this Advanced Micro Devices narrative.

Another View: Advanced Micro Devices Through The P/E Lens

Advanced Micro Devices screens very differently when you swap community fair value models for a simple P/E check. The stock trades on 117.4x earnings, compared with a 41.4x average for the US Semiconductor sector and a 54.3x fair ratio that the market could eventually move toward.

That spread points to a rich valuation rather than a discount, which means even small disappointments could bite harder than investors anchored on a $907.32 fair value might expect. Is this a premium you are comfortable paying for the current AI narrative, or a signal to demand more proof in the numbers?

AMD Is Up 127% in a Year. William Blair Just Upgraded It as Nvidia Loses Its CEO ©@undefined from Getty Images Pro via Canva, @Kittipong Jirasukhanont from PhonlamaiPhoto's Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

AMD stock rose 6% today after William Blair upgraded it to Outperform, on the same day Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang resigned and Nvidia was downgraded by several firms.

AMD's own numbers support the upgrade, and Nvidia's turmoil doesn't add much to it.

Analysts have raised their 2027 earnings estimate for AMD to $17.69 a share, from $15.33 three months ago.

The stock trades a little above its 5-year average forward P/E, and the $659 consensus target sits 12% above today's price.

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD:NASDAQ) is up 6% today, and two things are helping it. William Blair upgraded the stock to Outperform from Market Perform this morning, and Nvidia (NVDA:NASDAQ), its biggest rival in AI chips, lost its CEO.

Jensen Huang resigned, and KeyBanc, Melius and Evercore ISI all downgraded Nvidia, which fell 6%. AMD, already up 127% over the past year, kept climbing.

William Blair's case runs through AMD's own chips

William Blair says the risk/reward has shifted in AMD's favor, though it set no price target. It sees room for AMD's Instinct GPUs to gain share, and for its CPUs to win more work inside customers' custom chip programs. AMD CEO Lisa Su said on the third-quarter call that OpenAI picked AMD's EPYC processors as the host CPUs for its first custom accelerator platforms.

Third-quarter revenue grew 45% to $13.4 billion, Data Center revenue nearly doubled to $8.5 billion, and Su now expects revenue to grow more than 80% in 2027.

But "It is true that demand is higher than supply," Su said on the call. So customers spooked by Nvidia's boardroom can't move many 2027 orders to AMD in a hurry.

The numbers back the upgrade

The Street's consensus target has climbed from $272 a year ago to $659:

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)

That's 12% above today's price. Targets from the 53 analysts covering the stock run from $525 to $1,250.

The targets rose because the earnings estimates did. Analysts expect normalized EPS of $8.08 this year and $17.69 in 2027, up from $4.17 in 2025:

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2024-2028 (TIKR)

Three months ago, the 2027 estimate was $15.33.

AMD traded at 37x forward earnings at the last close. That's a bit above its 5-year average of 35x and far below the 67x it hit at the end of June:

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

Today's jump pushes it a little higher.

Nvidia's mess is the least of it

title: S&P 500 Recovered $1 Trillion in 90 Minutes Despite Wider Market Crash
detail:
S&P 500 Recovered $1 Trillion in 90 Minutes Despite Wider Market Crash
Jakub Dziadkowiec
Thu, November 12, 2026 at 2:14 PM MST 2 min read
NVDA
^GSPC
AMD
AVGO
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The S&P 500 looked headed for a bruising Thursday after Nvidia lost as much as $600 billion in market value. Then Wall Street reversed course.

The index fell nearly 1% at the opening bell as Nvidia shares plunged up to 14% following founder Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation. Within about 90 minutes, the S&P 500 had recovered its losses.

Why Didn't Nvidia Drag Down the Whole Market?

Nvidia's sell-off was severe, but it eased as trading progressed. Buyers also moved into its competitors: AMD rose roughly 7%, while Broadcom gained more than 5%.

Gains elsewhere helped offset Nvidia's losses, suggesting investors were still willing to bet on demand for AI chips, even as they questioned Nvidia's leadership.

Retail investors bought an estimated $111 million of Nvidia shares in the first half-hour alone, Reuters reported.

"You notice some of Nvidia's losses have been offset by gains in competitors," Peter Tuz, president of Chase Investment Counsel, told Reuters.

Nvidia has appointed finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO. Its next earnings report on November 17 will test whether customers' spending and growth expectations can withstand the leadership upheaval.

What Should Stock Market Investors Watch Next?

The S&P 500 rebound happened despite another warning sign: the 10-year US Treasury yield climbed above 5%, making borrowing more expensive.

Oil prices also rose after President Donald Trump hardened his position on Iran, adding to inflation worries.

On the chart, the S&P 500's immediate challenge is holding above roughly 7,624. A sustained move higher would put its record near 7,845 back in sight.

If selling returns, 7,484 is the first level to watch, followed by the November low near 7,350.

S&P 500 daily chart. Source: TradingView

Thursday showed that investors still want to buy market dips. Whether that enthusiasm survives higher yields and Nvidia's first earnings report without Huang remains the bigger question.

Analog Devices (ADI) and NVIDIA (NVDA) are both bought for the AI data center buildout, and the better buy depends on how much of your money you want on that one bet. NVIDIA made $89 billion of its $96 billion fiscal Q2 2027 revenue from data centers. At Analog Devices, management puts its AI exposure at about 20% of the company. That share counts its ATE and data center businesses together. So what did each company tell investors in August about the quarters ahead?

Analog Devices Expects Higher Margins, NVIDIA Expects Lower

Analog Devices told investors on August 19, 2026, that it expects its adjusted gross margin to rise to about 74% in fiscal Q4 2026, up from 72.5% in fiscal Q3. Management tied the gain to a better product mix, higher volumes and its own price increase, adding that the full effect of that price increase is not yet in the fiscal Q4 outlook.

The outlook from NVIDIA moved in the opposite direction. Memory prices rose more than management expected, leading the company to reset its margin outlook. NVIDIA now expects its gross margin to bottom at 71% to 72% in fiscal Q4 2027, down from 75% in fiscal Q2. The company's own price increases only take effect in fiscal Q1 2028.

Both companies guided revenue above the quarter they had just reported, meaning the two outlooks differ on profit rather than demand. Analog Devices is raising its prices now. NVIDIA is absorbing higher memory costs until its own price increases arrive.

Where NVIDIA And Analog Devices Spend Cash

NVIDIA is backing its own customers. Management said on the August 26, 2026 call that NVIDIA has invested nearly $50 billion in frontier AI labs, and that it expects AI labs it supports with its balance sheet to make up roughly a quarter of its business next year. Management also said it knows some will call this circular financing, though it said it sees the arrangements differently. That is the cost of NVIDIA's approach: more of its growth now depends on how those labs fare.

Analog Devices spends on acquisitions and shareholders. The company paid $1.5 billion in cash for Empower Semiconductor in July 2026, and in November 2026 completed its acquisition of Alif Semiconductor for $1.35 billion in cash plus up to $200 million in contingent payments, funded with part of a $3 billion bond sale in September. Management said it returned more than all of its free cash flow over the past twelve months to shareholders. On August 1, 2026, before that bond sale, Analog Devices owed $9.12 billion against $2.32 billion in cash and short-term investments.
